releases.notes:
EasyEconomy 1.1.0. Fabric 26.3, server-side only, Java 25, Geyser-friendly (Bedrock players use the same chest GUIs).

Gameplay feedback round on top of 1.0.2:

- Coins are money, not materials: refused in player crafting, the crafter block, the cartography table and villager and wandering trader trades. The crafter's redstone craft also refuses to fire while the grid holds a coin, and manual clicks and shift-moves can't place coins in it.
- Chest GUIs no longer freeze the player's own inventory. Shift-moves rebalance inside the player rows; drag-paint and double-click gather stay blocked.
- Closing a GUI with an item on the cursor returns it to the player (or drops it) instead of losing it.
- Menu titles are styled (gold, bold, optional pack glyph via guiTitleBadge). Item names, lore and menu feedback are capitalized and punctuated.
- Challenge completion shows a vanilla advancement toast, completions are logged, and an advancement earned before the challenge existed no longer auto-completes it on the first poll.
- The resource pack now covers the GUI title badge (font and texture).

Evidence and scope limits: independent QA accepted the final fix (a075336 content, landed as 83116ad) after rejecting the first 1.1.0 build for two bugs (GUI could eat a held item, crafter could use coins), both fixed. For this release the jar was rebuilt from 83116ad with ./gradlew build, which passed the 43 economy-core and 179 transaction assertions. The in-game selftest (booted headless server, 107 checks plus restart persistence) was run by the author on the same code before the final QA fix and was not re-run for the tag. Bedrock/Geyser-native forms are still deferred.

releases.notes:
EasyEconomy 1.0.2 — first public release. Fabric 26.3, server-side only, Java 25, Geyser-friendly (Bedrock players use the same chest GUIs).

Balances, /pay, /eco, physical currency items with /withdraw and /deposit, a configurable server shop with per-player buy limits, player-to-player shops with journaled escrow and crash recovery, and stat-based challenges with rewards. Storage is JSON in the config folder; the optional built-in pack server is off by default.

1.0.2 adds hardening fixes from independent review: saves fail closed when an unreadable accounts file cannot be preserved, balances decode per row with malformed rows skipped (strict integers), autosave tick math uses wide arithmetic with a sane bound, and invalid config values fall back coherently.

Safety model: money moves are durable-or-rolled-back; deliveries are verified by reading the saved player file back (vanilla's save swallows write failures, so the read-back is the only proof). Crash recovery is loss-biased in the measured windows: a crash can lose an item or coins, never duplicate them; every such window logs loudly for an admin. A single /withdraw is capped at 100,000,000; withdraws that cannot fit the main inventory are refused instead of spilling.

Evidence and scope limits, stated honestly:
- Independent QA: bounded source and failure-fix review over multiple rounds (final ACCEPT on 1e6ae3f, after ce324a3 scored 9.1; this release adds only the version string). QA's native-service probes exercised the real services, PlayerSaves, command methods and native Inventory/serialization with controlled snapshot/save/load and spawn boundaries, not a booted server, live playerdata IO, or real crash races.
- Author-run: 179 transaction assertions (crash injected at every step of list/buy/cancel, restart + recovery, forced write failures), 43 economy-core assertions (including an 8-thread transfer race), integration suite booting a real headless server with two fake players (92 checks through the real command dispatcher and menus, 6 post-restart persistence checks), clean-boot test.
